clue.text: Downright dull

blocks.note: first meaning: utterly or completely
second meaning: lifeless and flat, as a dull party or colour

explanation.walkthrough: The pair reads like a judgement that something is downright dull, but the two words are separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb the word means completely or utterly, and as an adjective it means lacking liveliness or sparkle.

clue.text: Shoots game

blocks.note: first meaning: moves suddenly and quickly
second meaning: the pub game of throwing small arrows at a board

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoots game' suggests hunting, but the clue is two separate meanings of one word: a verb of sudden movement and a pub game.
explanation.definitionFit: To dart is to move suddenly and swiftly, and the plural noun names the familiar board-and-arrows pub pastime.

clue.text: Princess tied to rock stars in group

blocks.note: first meaning: the Ethiopian princess of Greek myth chained to a rock as an offering to a sea monster
second meaning: the constellation named after her

explanation.surface: A princess of rock royalty is linked to a band full of famous stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' and 'stars in group' suggest a pop band, but the rock is a literal sea rock and the stars are a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Perseus rescued this chained princess, and the northern constellation bearing her name is a recognised group of stars.

clue.text: Here peers sit, in Lords, returned to power

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the House of Lords is the upper chamber of Parliament
taken as written
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: A note on where members of the House of Lords sit, a party having been returned to power.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a pun: 'peers' are not nobles but people who pee, read as pee-ers. TO plus P, read backwards, gives POT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedroom receptacle kept for urinating at night is literally a place where those relieving themselves sit.

clue.text: Proclaimed leader corrupt in high definition!

indicators.note: corrupted material has been altered and spoilt from its proper form, so the letters are rearranged
one thing set in another sits inside it, so these letters go within the outer pair

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
HD is the standard abbreviation for high definition, as on televisions

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a crooked leader being announced in crisp high-definition broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corrupt' reads as an adjective describing the leader, but it is the signal to rearrange that word's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A herald announced news publicly, so to herald something is to proclaim or announce it; the past tense matches.

clue.text: Doctor on boat in capital

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another sits above it, so they join in that order

blocks.note: MO is a Medical Officer, an army doctor
a scow is a flat-bottomed boat

explanation.surface: A doctor is aboard a vessel moored in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: A scow is a flat-bottomed barge, a word met more often in crosswords than on rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian seat of government is the country's chief city, which is what capital means here.

clue.text: Ena holding youngster eats a hot snack

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it within your grasp, so one piece goes inside the other
whatever is eaten ends up inside the eater, so one piece swallows the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a youngster is a child
taken as written

explanation.surface: Granny Ena watches a child tuck into a spicy snack.
explanation.walkthrough: Two nested containers: the child takes in A first, and that whole unit then sits between EN and A.
explanation.definitionFit: This Mexican dish is a rolled tortilla with a chilli sauce, so it is a hot, spicy bite to eat.

clue.text: No serious accident: police initially called

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the word is used

blocks.note: the first letter of police
rang means telephoned, i.e. called

explanation.surface: A minor bump on the road, but the police were called first anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: Prang is British slang for a minor car crash or bump.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang this word means a minor collision in a car, which is exactly a crash that is not serious.

clue.text: Time passed with that European card game

indicators.note: with means alongside or together, so the pieces are simply joined one after the next

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
went is past tense of go, so passed by
yon is an old or dialect word for that one over there
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Time slipped by while playing a card game with a European.
explanation.walkthrough: YON is an archaic or dialect word for 'that', common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: This gambling game, also called blackjack or pontoon, is named after the score players try to reach without going bust.

clue.text: Ilsa in Casablanca, Lima and in Berlin

blocks.note: Lima is the NATO alphabet word for L
und is German for and

explanation.surface: A film character listed alongside the capitals Lima and Berlin, like a travel itinerary.
explanation.walkthrough: Lima and Berlin look like cities but one is the radio-alphabet letter and the other tells you to translate into German.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingrid Bergman played Ilsa, whose full name in the 1942 film is Ilsa Lund, so the surname completes the character.

clue.text: Maoists argued furiously blocking road south

indicators.note: doing something furiously means doing it wildly and chaotically, so the letters are scrambled
something blocking a passage sits in the middle of it, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
Rd is the abbreviation for road
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Militants argue heatedly while blocking a road heading south.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters sit inside RD, with S added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Guards were the student militias who served Mao Zedong during China's Cultural Revolution, so they were Maoists.

clue.text: Refrain from church when finally contrite

indicators.note: finally means at the very end, so only the closing letter of the word is used

blocks.note: CE is the Church of England
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
the last letter of contrite

explanation.surface: A repentant churchgoer finally holds back from something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refrain' tempts as a noun, a song's chorus, but it is the verb meaning to hold back.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain is to stop yourself doing something, and to cease is to stop, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Leader of soldiers, given news, means to fight

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter of the next word is taken
given means supplied with something extra, so the next piece is added on

blocks.note: the first letter of soldiers
word can mean news, as in 'any word from them?'

explanation.surface: A commander of troops receives news and decides it is reason to go to war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Means to fight' sounds like a motive, but it is a noun phrase: the means, or weapon, with which one fights.
explanation.definitionFit: A bladed weapon is a classic instrument of combat, which is what a means to fight describes.

clue.text: See 26
Soused Democrat forced to renounce whiskey

indicators.note: to renounce something is to give it up, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for Democrat
wrenched means pulled or forced violently
Whiskey is the NATO alphabet word for W

explanation.surface: A drunken politician is made to give up whiskey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soused' suggests drunk, fitting the whiskey, but here it means soaked through; whiskey is just the letter W.
explanation.definitionFit: Soused can mean thoroughly soaked in liquid, the same as being wet through by a downpour.

clue.text: Libertine in uniform somehow breached walls

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so these letters are arranged in some other order
walls enclose a space, so these letters surround the other piece

blocks.note: Uniform is the NATO alphabet word for U
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rake dressed in uniform has somehow broken through the walls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Walls' looks like the object of 'breached', but it is a verb: the rearranged letters wall in U.
explanation.definitionFit: A libertine is a dissolute person given to excess, the same as one who corrupts or indulges in debauchery.

clue.text: Differences in Nicaraguan rebels crossing street

indicators.note: something crossing a path lies across its middle, so these letters sit within the other piece

blocks.note: the Contras were US-backed rebels in 1980s Nicaragua
St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Rifts among Nicaraguan guerrillas as they cross a street.
explanation.walkthrough: The Contras were the rebel force that fought Nicaragua's Sandinista government in the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrasts are noticeable dissimilarities between things, so the plural noun is a synonym for differences.

clue.text: Look old taking book inside summerhouse

indicators.note: taking something in means accepting it within, so one piece goes inside
inside confirms the placement within the surrounding letters

blocks.note: to gaze is to look steadily
B is the abbreviation for book
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An old person reading a book in the garden summerhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look old' reads as 'appear aged', but the words are separate pieces, with the book slipped between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazebo is a small open garden pavilion, which is what a summerhouse is.

clue.text: Just English left on rising Italian island

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another sits above it, so they join in that order
in a down clue rising means read upwards, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
quit means left, as in 'quit the room'
Elba is the Italian island where Napoleon was exiled

explanation.surface: An Englishman has just set off for an Italian island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like the adverb 'only', but the definition is the adjective meaning fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Just as an adjective means fair and impartial, the same quality described by the answer.

clue.text: Detectives wait on southern swells

blocks.note: DIs are Detective Inspectors
to tend is to look after or wait on someone
S is the abbreviation for southern

explanation.surface: Police officers wait for some well-dressed southern gentlemen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swells' looks like a noun for smart toffs, but it is the verb meaning expands.
explanation.definitionFit: To distend is to bulge outwards from internal pressure, so the third-person verb is a synonym for swells.

clue.text: Rick in Casablanca and Abilene endlessly drunk

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off
a drunk staggers about unsteadily, so these letters fall into a jumbled order

blocks.note: the Texas town loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Humphrey Bogart's character drinking his way through a Texas cowtown.
explanation.walkthrough: Abilene is a town in Texas and Kansas, used only for its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Humphrey Bogart's role in the 1942 film is the nightclub owner Rick Blaine, so the surname identifies him.

clue.text: Horrible Gaultier tie

indicators.note: something horrible is a mess, so these letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the fashion designer's surname supplies the letters

explanation.surface: A fashion critic sneers at a hideous necktie from designer Jean Paul Gaultier.
explanation.walkthrough: The surname of the French designer is just a set of letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A ligature is a cord or band used for binding, so it is a thing that ties, a synonym for tie.

clue.text: See 26
Top meal without starter succeeded in test

indicators.note: with no starter means the opening letter is taken off
one thing set in another sits inside it, so these letters go within the other piece

blocks.note: supper is an evening meal
S is the abbreviation for succeeded
the MOT is Britain's annual roadworthiness test for cars

explanation.surface: A top-quality dinner, minus its first course, passed the inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' suggests the first course of a meal, but it means the first letter; the MOT is Britain's yearly roadworthiness test for vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppermost means highest in position or rank, which is what top means as an adjective.

clue.text: Old man covers chest in warm coat

indicators.note: a covering wraps round what it protects, so these letters go outside the other piece

blocks.note: pa is a familiar word for father, one's old man
an ark is a chest or box, as in the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: An elderly man wraps his chest up in a warm coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chest' reads as part of the body, but it is a storage box.
explanation.definitionFit: A parka is a hooded, padded jacket for cold weather, so it is a warm coat.

clue.text: Where the young go crazy

blocks.note: first meaning: a small chamber pot for toddlers being toilet trained
second meaning: British informal for mad or foolish

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a hip hangout where young people go wild; 'go' is the toddler's euphemism for using the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a child's training toilet, and the British adjective means slightly mad or crazy.

clue.text: Fairy Liquid's top removed from bottle

indicators.note: the top of a word is its opening letter, so just that one is taken
something removed is taken away, so that letter is dropped from the other word

blocks.note: the first letter of liquid
bottle is British slang for courage, as is pluck

explanation.surface: The cap of a washing-up liquid bottle has been taken off.
explanation.walkthrough: Fairy Liquid is a British washing-up liquid brand, but the words split: bottle is British slang for nerve or courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Puck is the mischievous sprite in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, so he is a famous example of a fairy.

clue.text: Wait up to welcome eastern poet

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards
to welcome a guest is to take them in, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: to stay is to wait or remain
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: Someone stays up late to greet a poet from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wait up' reads as a phrase meaning stay awake, but 'up' is the turnaround signal.
explanation.definitionFit: W. B. Yeats was the Irish Nobel laureate who wrote The Second Coming, so he is a well-known poet.

clue.text: South Korean yogi liked nutty 19 Across's line for 9 Down

indicators.note: nutty means crazy, so the preceding letters are rearranged in a mad order

blocks.note: all twenty letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A meditation guru from Seoul enjoyed a crazy quotation from a classic film.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to the other two Casablanca clues: Rick Blaine's famous toast to Ilsa Lund.
explanation.definitionFit: Bogart's character repeatedly toasts Bergman's with this phrase in the 1942 film, making it his signature line to her.

clue.text: Reptile, one ruling civil contingencies committee

blocks.note: a king is one who rules
COBRA is the UK government's emergency committee, named after Cabinet Office Briefing Room A

explanation.surface: A cold-blooded creature chairs the government's emergency meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: COBRA is the British government's crisis committee, which meets in Cabinet Office Briefing Room A.
explanation.definitionFit: The king cobra is the world's longest venomous snake, so it is a specific example of a reptile.

clue.text: Musician knocks poet capturing hearts

indicators.note: to capture is to seize and hold, so these letters close around another

blocks.note: raps are sharp knocks
an odist is a writer of odes
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games

explanation.surface: A musician criticises a poet who wins people's affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocks' reads as 'criticises' and 'hearts' as affections, but they are raps and the card-suit abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhapsodist composes or performs rhapsodies, free and emotional musical pieces, so is a kind of musician.

clue.text: Olympian from Egyptian port returned

indicators.note: something returned goes back where it came from, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: Suez is the Egyptian port at the southern end of the Suez Canal

explanation.surface: An Olympic athlete comes home from a port in Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Olympian' suggests a Games athlete, but it means one of the gods of Mount Olympus.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeus was king of the Greek gods who lived on Mount Olympus, so he is the chief Olympian.
